description: Fail-closed inventory for failure drills. Component fault injection, local CI system-boundary drills and production chaos are different evidence classes and may not be relabeled. Exact-source CI currently executes API graceful interruption and parser restart-after-failure. Database failover, object-store outage and mixed-version failure remain unexecuted production-blocking gaps.

requiredAssertions: real loopback TCP listener accepts an in-flight request
Shutdown does not return before the active request completes
the active request preserves its successful response
Serve exits with http.ErrServerClosed
new requests are rejected after shutdown
limitations: not a load-balancer or multi-instance drain
does not prove client retry behavior

requiredAssertions: truncated worker output is rejected
the failed attempt leaves no spool residue
the same manager and spool ID can be reused
the replacement worker seals a valid result
independent verification matches recovered evidence
limitations: Linux CI with the test worker artifact
not a production parser deployment restart
does not yet cover timeout, CPU, memory and host-restart combinations as a matrix

requiredAssertions: requests fail closed during database unavailability
no cross-tenant or partial mutation occurs
recovery does not revive expired sessions or deleted accounts
lease and retry state resumes without duplicate effects
recovery-point and role/RLS invariants are independently verified
limitations: no failover or loss drill exists

requiredAssertions: authorization and completion fail closed during outage
no object version is silently substituted
queued work resumes idempotently
checksum and metadata binding survive recovery
ambiguous object state is quarantined rather than deleted
limitations: local exact-version restore is not an outage drill

requiredAssertions: old and current backends coexist against expanded schema
persisted jobs and previews remain readable by supported versions
unsupported release order fails before mutation
rollback target remains deployable
contract migration is blocked until old-version drain is proven
limitations: compatibility policy exists but no executable mixed-version failure drill exists
